spatial_entity.notes: Reuses the existing reviewed New Kingdom spatial identity and time-sliced geometry. Political extent does not imply uniform slave prevalence or identical legal status across all dependent populations.

claim.summary: Specialist Egyptological synthesis identifies the New Kingdom as a period of large-scale foreign enslavement associated with military campaigns and also documents locally owned or rented servitude. The terminology and legal status of Egyptian dependents were heterogeneous, so the atlas records positive slavery/enslavement while keeping servants, conscripts, corvée labour and foreign war captives analytically distinct and assigning no new post-M1 P-level.
claim.notes: Reconciles legacy claim 7cd1da37-b2f8-4dba-b63b-9cffa6e19b65. Legacy P3 remains historical metadata only.

territorial_practice.notes: Positive classification with terminology controls. Do not equate all bAk/Hm, corvée or state labour with slavery.

source.title: Slavery and Servitude
source.independence_notes: Specialist Egyptological synthesis with explicit historical differentiation among coercive labour, servants and slavery.
source.reliability_limitations: Broad synthesis; Egyptian status terminology is heterogeneous and cannot be normalized mechanically to modern slavery categories.
